key_insight: Generating a plausible synthetic PV history from site metadata and weather lets time-series foundation models make strong cold-start forecasts before any real target-site measurements exist.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical commissioning-time forecasting workflow for new photovoltaic plants, reducing the need to wait for historical production data while improving early operational planning.
method: Create synthetic production histories from plant metadata plus meteorological covariates.
Condition five time-series foundation models at inference time on the synthetic context.
Benchmark against classical baselines under Cold-Start Baseline, Real Feedback, and Self-Forecast Feedback settings.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates 440 PV sites across four datasets and finds covariate-aware foundation models outperform baselines by about 1.7–2×, with TabPFN-TS best under Real Feedback and Chronos-2 most robust under Self-Forecast Feedback.
watch_item: The approach depends on having plausible metadata and weather covariates, and the gains appear tied more to the presence of synthetic temporal context than to the specific history generator.
paper_title: Time series Foundation Models based on Physics-Informed Synthetic Histories for Cold-Start Photovoltaic Forecasting
